notes: Truthful preparation pitch, with a neutral synthetic narrator. User confirmed solo developer Gyu-min Kim. SLIME CEO! is only the upload channel, not developer/team identity. Relevant biography, user research and public payout proof remain unprovided. Rewrite current-status lines only after those facts change.

shots.title: Problem, product and creator
shots.narration: Giveaways attract a crowd. DROP turns the reward into something they can play. I'm Gyu-min Kim, the creator of DROP. I'm building for Telegram KOLs and community operators running an AMA, a launch, or a thank you event. The customer hypothesis: keep participation playful and make each promised reward accountable.

shots.title: Actual consumer games and planned settlement
shots.narration: The public website already offers two short games and five languages, with English as the default. The intended reward flow adds one sign in, a server verified result, and a funded Monad escrow. The server checks the game. The blockchain settles an authorized fixed reward. Testnet tokens have no financial value.

shots.title: Why Monad and prototype stage
shots.narration: Monad is the settlement layer: the fixed reward budget and payment can be inspected, while the participant sees a game and a receipt. We're at the working testnet prototype stage. This preparation footage is unpaid practice; the final payment flow will be shown only after its actual receipt is verified.

shots.title: Concrete proposed first pilot
shots.narration: Our next pilot observes five people without Monad wallets and interviews ten operators. We'll measure unaided completion, confirmed receipt, recovery, and repeat events. The first hundred participant target is five pilot creators inviting twenty people each. These are future targets, not existing partners. DROP: playable participation, verifiable rewards.
